name: cua_run_code
title: Computer use program
description: Run a TypeScript program to observe and operate desktop applications. The global cua object is ready to use; retain application and window objects across calls. Only tools.cua is available inside the program. Call other session tools directly. Print the values you need or leave a final expression; screenshots are attached after the program finishes. The program contains TypeScript REPL statements; only erasable syntax is accepted, with no enum or namespaces. Type annotations are advisory. Top-level declarations and await are supported; top-level return is not supported. Emit output with console.log(...) or a final lossless JSON expression. Only printed values and that final expression become program output. Variables, functions, and imported modules remain in memory for this Agent across calls. Use await import(...) for modules. Direct filesystem access follows the environment's launch-time sandbox policy; process.env starts empty. Timeout and cancellation results say whether retained variables were preserved or cleared. Restart, sandbox changes, output overflow, or process failure clears them. Recreate missing variables and resources; conversation history does not restore state. Earlier mutations and tool effects are not rolled back. Approved sandbox escalations use a fresh environment and discard its variables afterward. Do not redeclare existing let, const, or class names; reuse mutable bindings or choose new names. Await tools and cleanup before returning; unfinished tools reject. After completion, timeout, or cancellation, new tool calls are rejected and captured output is discarded; background work may still change state. Await child-process completion before returning; raw output belongs to the active evaluation. Each program starts in the Session's current directory. Running programs keep their initial directory. A sandbox escalation approves this complete program for one execution only. Nested tools retain their own policies and approvals. Request wider access only after evidence of a denial. Earlier effects may already have completed: inspect them before explicitly retrying. Programs are never replayed automatically.

code.description: The TypeScript program to execute, following this tool's execution instructions.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this program does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "Count TODO markers across packages"; "Read failing test and its fixture"; "Rename config key in every cordis.yml".

timeoutMs.description: Positive elapsed-time budget in milliseconds, including nested tool and approval waits. Default 120000; capped at 600000. Zero does not disable the deadline.

name: cua_reset
title: Reset computer use program state
description: Discard the program environment of this connection: every variable, import, and application or window object held by earlier cua_run_code calls. Application access grants and the desktop applications themselves are unaffected; the next cua_run_code call starts a fresh environment and its result repeats the `cua` API reference. Use it when a declaration conflicts with an earlier call or the environment has become unusable.
